content: ABCD3, also known as ATP-binding cassette sub-family D member 3, is a protein encoded by the ABCD3 gene in humans. This protein belongs to the ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter superfamily, which is responsible for transporting various molecules across cellular and intracellular membranes. ABC transporters are categorized into seven distinct subfamilies: ABC1, MDR/TAP, MRP, ALD, OABP, GCN20, and White. ABCD3 is specifically a member of the ALD subfamily. The ALD subfamily is involved in the transport of fatty acids and/or fatty acyl-CoAs into peroxisomes, which are essential organelles for lipid metabolism and other cellular processes. All known peroxisomal ABC transporters, including ABCD3, are half-transporters. This means they require another half-transporter molecule to form a functional transporter, which can be either a homodimer (two identical subunits) or a heterodimer (two different subunits). ABCD3 is a peroxisomal membrane protein that is believed to play a critical role in the biogenesis of peroxisomes. Clinically, mutations in the ABCD3 gene have been linked to certain forms of Zellweger syndrome. Zellweger syndrome is a group of disorders characterized by defects in peroxisome assembly, leading to a wide range of metabolic and developmental abnormalities.
